A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, and unmasked universality construction. All 16 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices and mathematical displays, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical definitions, approximation results, and proofs. Section 2.3 discusses training and applications conceptually but reports no original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added masked-attention results, including Appendix C, are theorems and proofs rather than experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

M1.justification: The underlying attention–MLP construction remains. The masked layer already sketched in v1 Eq. (11) is revised: v2 Eq. (12) uses source times r≤t instead of the printed t≤t', and includes a residual term. Eq. (13) also specifies composition that preserves timestamps. These are limited procedural refinements alongside the substantial theoretical extension.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or tasks. References to vision, NLP, and time series describe potential applications; the added causal theory does not establish empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither PDF evaluates comparison methods against a proposed implementation. Discussed transformer architectures and universality results are related work, not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. The new regularity assumptions and architectural bounds concern mathematical approximation results.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, error analyses, or empirical case studies. The additional appendix material consists of mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty. Their approximation-error bounds are deterministic theoretical statements.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains empirical performance values, rankings, or observed qualitative findings. The newly reported formal results are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 2 on causal masked universality, definitions of Lipschitz contexts, masked measures, causal identifiable maps, and reduced mappings. Section 4 and Appendix C add arguments concerning continuity, compactness, composition, and preservation of identifiability under uniform approximation. v1's unmasked theorem and constructive proof are retained and reorganized in Section 3 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly leaves masked attention outside its universality result. v2's abstract, contributions, and conclusion claim coverage of both unmasked and causal masked transformers, with Theorem 2 restricted to continuous causal identifiable targets on the specified Lipschitz contexts. The existing claims about token-count independence and bounded embedding dimensions remain.

C2.justification: The exclusion of masked attention is replaced by substantive applicability qualifications: temporal Wasserstein-Lipschitz regularity, identifiability, and minimum initial-time mass. Section 4.1 discusses why these assumptions matter, the exclusion of measures with densities under the atom requirement, and an alternative with a fixed time marginal. The limitations concerning quantitative bounds and head-count dependence remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3, Remark 4 newly explains that the constructed context-free blocks can be realized exactly when MLPs represent identity maps, as with ReLU, and otherwise require further approximation. This adds construction detail without documenting an implemented experiment or providing code, hardware, or data-access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds mathematical references by Aliprantis and Border, Boman and Lindskog, Kelley, and Santambrogio, while removing the Fornasier–Sodini–Savaré citation motivating cylindrical functions. The comparisons with earlier transformer-universality work remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing exposition is substantially reorganized: background notation moves into Appendix A, and the lengthy unmasked proof becomes a shorter main-text argument with details in Appendix B. The training/application subsection is removed, the scalar approximation argument is rewritten, and separate masked-theory sections and proofs are introduced.

P2.justification: The unnumbered construction diagram moves from v1 Section 3.3 to v2 Appendix B.3 and receives revised notation. Mathematical displays are reflowed within the reorganized text, while the single-column visual format remains. No empirical tables or plotted figures are added.

improvement.justification: v2 reorganizes the existing proof and tackles v1's explicitly deferred causal setting, but the central addition has a material proof gap. An allowed context with a constant spatial token and equal time masses at 0 and 1/2 makes the masked measure jump at 1/2 under Eq. (19), contradicting Lemma 10's continuity assertion. Appendix C.3 also assumes convergence across such cutoffs. The benefits of the revision therefore coexist with unresolved support for its main new theorem, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
